recipes.name: No Time to Cook Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of celery soup

steps.text: Place chicken breasts in a slow cooker. In a medium bowl, mix the cream of chicken soup and cream of celery soup until smooth Pour over the chicken, making sure it is well coated.
Cover, and cook on Low heat for 7 to 8 hours. Stir in the sour cream about 1/2 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: No Time to Cook Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Canned soups and sour cream blend into a smooth sauce for chicken in this crock pot recipe.

review.reviewBody:
If I would have made this recipe exactly as stated, I'm sure it wouldn't have turned out so great, like other reviewers have commented. 

However - I made a couple modifications and it turned out absolutely EXCELLENT! I made the base recipe following the original instructions, except I seasoned the chicken with garlic salt, pepper and paprika. I sliced up a white onion, (not chopped) placed half the onion slices in the bottom of the crockpot, placed the chicken on top, then put the rest of the onions on top of the chicken. I mixed low fat crm of mush. soup & crm of chicken soup in a bowl, added a little milk until it was smooth, and then mixed in a can of diced tomatos & a can of sliced mushrooms. I poured that over the chicken and onions, and sprinkled garlic salt, pepper and paprika on the top of everything. Since it was just for me and my husband, I only use 3 pieces of boneless, skinless chicken breasts. I turned the crockpot on high, it only took 2 1/2 to cook. I served over egg noodles. 

I'm not kidding. This is one of the BEST dinners I have ever made! The sauce was excellent and the chicken was really really moist and tender. My husband basically licked his plate, and as I'm writing this review, he's over there eating another helping!

Made as directed along with some suggestions from reviewers. 1) Sprinkled onion powder, paprika, and pepper on chicken before putting in crock pot. Put chopped onions and minced garlic under the chicken. Only used 2 boneless, skinless chicken breasts so cooked on high for 2 1/2 hours. Used cream of celery, cream of mushroom (since I was out of cream of chicken) and added about a tablespoon of powdered chicken bouillon). Served over mashed potatoes w/sides of corn and peas. I don't eat meat but my husband does. He LOVED it. I loved the gravy on the mashed potatoes! Will definitely add to my rotation!

This was quite good and I too made some additions and subtractions like some of the others here. I'm mainly reviewing this so I can remember what I did for the next time I cook this. I used cream of celery and cream of mushroom, added sliced onion and chopped one rib of celery since I had it. I also added two carrots, chopped as well. Forgot the sour cream. Added a drained can of fire roasted diced tomatoes with garlic, and added more minced garlic. Added maybe a tsp of oregano, and a liberal amount of black pepper. Shredded the chicken about 2 hours prior to serving, and added a can of cut up white potatoes to it about 1 hour before. Served with Zatarans Yellow Rice. Giving 4 stars due to all my changes, but my version was DELICIOUS.

Very good--my hubby came back for seconds pretty quickly. I followed the advice of a few others--I used frozen chicken breasts. I seasoned the chicken w/ garlic-pepper seasoning, used cream of chicken & cream of mushroom soups (had no cream of celery), a can of mushrooms & a little bit of french-fried onions. I cooked it on high for 3 hours, added the sour cream & turned it to low for about 30 mins. Served over angel hair pasta w/ a side of green beans. Will definitely make again.

I have had this recipe saved for a long time. And this was awesome I used way more chicken then the recommendation and will probably double the soups for more gravy. Served it over rice and veggies and it was a hit. Only change was I used thinner breast put it on for 6 hours and my husband shredded the chicken lightly mid way thru delicious!!!

This sounds like a simple base recipe... So I assume you could go in many different directions from here. Thank you for giving me a place to start. I just threw in three boneless chicken breasts seasoned with garlic powder, Onion powder, smoked paprika, and a dash of kosher salt. Next I mixed the cream of celery and cream of chicken with a splash of 2% milk and set it aside while I chopped my vegetables. Fresh white button mushroom, green pepper, red pepper, and garden fresh tomatoes all look beautiful together... I hope it will taste as good as it looks! Guess I'll have to run to the store for some sour cream though, huh?

Awesome! I made it just the way Michelle McCormick did, added a can of tomatoes, a can of mushrooms, some sliced onion and seasoned the chicken with pepper and garlic salt. Served over egg noodles, IT WAS AWESOME!! A great go-to recipe, quick, cheap, and you have everything in the house already. I will definitely make this again.
Delicious I used cream of mushroom cream of celery and sour cream mixed all together and covered chicken cooked 6 hours it was great I did add salt pepper and garlic salt then served over egg noodles

Delicious with tweaks. 8 added French broccoli and cauliflower and onions and tomatoes and seasoned the chicken with garlic salt and hardcore carnivore pork and chicken seasoning. Served it with Basmati rice. Excellent

As it turns out, I got the chance to use up a lot of canned foods I had lying around for this recipe - what a hit!! I used cream of mushroom and a can of turkey gravy. I used chicken thighs instead of chicken breasts, and two small onions (as recommended by other users) sliced thick on the bottom and on top of the chicken. I added a bit of milk to the liquid mixture, and a strained can of diced tomatoes. I didn't add the sour cream at the end (I forgot :/) and then I served it with steamed vegetables and mashed potatoes! Everyone loved it! Very filling! I cooked it on high, and it was perfect right around 4 1/2, 5 hours. I will definitely make it again!

This was very good, but I followed other's suggestions and used cream of mushroom soup in place of cream of celery. I also added a can of diced tomatoes, fresh mushrooms and onions. It turned out delicious. The one thing that I would do differently is shred the chicken about an hour before serving in order to let the flavors seep into the chicken more effectively.
The primary reason for this rating is that I made Michelle McCormick’s version. Let me say - it was one of the best meals I’ve ever made. Thank you so much for sharing, Michelle!
I'm giving it 4 stars as I made it using Michelle McCormick's recipe. As the recipe stands I'm sure it would have been bland.

Easy and delicious It came out a bit soupy, but serving it over rice helped Oh, I should admit that I couldn't find cream of celery soup at any of the stores (I checked them all in our little town of 4k) so I used cream of mushroom instead We live far awy from a "big" city so next time I'll do my best to find cream of celery and report back.
Love easy peasy four ingredient dinners - serve it alongside wild rice quinoa or in a loaf of french bread cut down the middle.
Easy and tastes great. I served over rice.

Great for little kids because it isn’t spicy. The next day I added leftover noodles, chicken, Carrot chips, and lots of chicken stock to the sauce and turned it into chicken noodle soup. They loved it.
I made no changes, I would make this again!
This recipe is so easy and so very good! Served over bow tie pasta is one of my husband's favorites. This will be in the line up forever.
Added in herbs, as others suggested, and it was a hit with my family.
